findings.finding: The Q2 quarter is pre-visible: monthly commissions Jul 2,638 / Aug 2,255 / Sep 1,798m yen sum to 6,691m (Q1 8,440m; Q2 last year about 5,822m), FX revenue 497/549/618m, margin long balance 478-517bn; implied Q2 net income about 5.0bn yen, -10% QoQ but about +37% YoY, so H1 headline (about 10.6bn vs 6.5bn) prints as a large YoY increase.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prints with monthly-visible quarters moved small: Q2 FY3/26 (2025-10-29) +1.2%, Q3 (2026-01-28/02-03) +1.4%, FY (2026-04-27) +2.0%, Q1 (2026-07-28, released 11:30) -0.8% close-to-close (Yahoo daily chart).
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: every component is in the monthlies the market has had since 1 Oct. Sized near 0; the only residual is the SG&A/financial-income line which the monthlies do not give, worth a fraction of a point either way.
findings.independence: July figures from a separate monthly release, https://www.matsui.co.jp/company/press/pdf/pr260803_2.pdf (same company series, so not independent evidence about the reaction).

findings.finding: The interim dividend of 28 yen was pre-announced on 2026-08-26 under a new 'payout ratio 70% or more' policy and is formally resolved at this board; at an estimated H1 EPS of about 41 yen, 28 yen is about 68% payout, so a 1-yen top-up to 29 at formal resolution is possible though not stated.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-08-26 interim announcement (after close) moved the stock +4.7% (1127->1180) and +2.6% the next day (1211): the dividend line is this name's biggest mover, but it is already out. Historically interims ran far above the floor (FY3/26 interim 25 yen on H1 EPS 25.38; FY3/25 22 on 23.69).
findings.why_not_priced: The 28 yen is priced (the stock jumped on it in August). What is not priced is a change at formal resolution: if H1 EPS lands above 40 yen, 28 yen falls below the stated 70% floor, which the market can only check once H1 net income is printed. Most likely outcome is 28 confirmed (zero), hence the small expected size.
findings.independence: Policy change to a 70% payout floor with DOE dropped is in the FY3/26 tanshin, https://www.matsui.co.jp/company/ir/pdf/2026_4.pdf (same issuer, different document); no external source on whether the board will top up.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-01 a monthly magazine reported the Matsui founding family (about 51% via asset-management companies) was exploring a sale of its stake, with SBI HD and large financials named as possible buyers; the stock rose +3.6% that day; there is no company confirmation, and the H1 print is the first briefing (決算説明会 held at H1, not at Q1) at which management may be asked.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance on this name; the rumour day itself moved +3.6% (1092->1131) and the gain has since been given back in absolute terms (1022 at 10/27), though Matsui is still about 4 points better than peers (Monex/SBI -10%) since 9/30.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the relative outperformance against peers since 9/30 suggests a few points of residual premium remain. A denial or 'no fact decided' comment at the briefing would remove some of it; silence (Matsui's usual practice) leaves it. Expected value slightly negative and small because the most likely outcome is no statement.
findings.independence: Same Fisco story syndicated at https://www.moneypost.jp/1451071; no independent confirmation from the company, the family or SBI.

outside_window.finding: October 2026 monthly (commissions, margin balance) is published around 2026-11-02; the Nikkei fell about 10% from its 6 Oct peak (70,684 to 62,190 on 10/26) and listed peer brokers fell 10%+, which points to weaker October activity and margin balances.

Strongest positive the release could carry is a dividend top-up or a first buyback; I looked, there is no buyback precedent and the top-up is a small possibility, so the sign tilts barely positive.
